title: DarkSword and Coruna iOS exploits continue to attack crypto wallets
content:
Macworld

A new report by security researchers at Censys warns that the DarkSword exploit on iOS continues to be used in conjunction with Coruna malware to steal cryptocurrency wallets. Discovered earlier this year, DarkSword/Coruna is a dual-edged hacking toolkit. DarkSword attacks WebKit and JavaScriptCore to access iOS’s SpringBoard that managing app launch and the Home screen. Coruna is the payload used to steal crypto wallet information.

Censys’ research found several servers that had DarkSword/Coruna deployment directories. Wallet apps being targeted include Bitpie, Coinbase, Exodus, imToken, MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, Uniswap, and OKEx. According to the site’s researchers, the exploit’s main purpose is wallet theft and also “mines Photos and Notes for BIP39 recovery phrases.”

As we reported back in March, old versions of iOS are vulnerable to DarkSword. All of the security holes used by DarkSword have been fixed as of iOS 26.3 (the current version is iOS 27.0.1). Users of older versions of iOS 26, iOS 18, and earlier may be vulnerable.

How to protect your iPhone from malware

The easiest task to perform to secure your iPhone is to update the operating system. iOS can be updated in the Settings app by tapping General > Software Update. Apple also has a separate method for installing immediate security patches called Background Security Improvements. It is located in Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the bottom to find Background Security Improvements. Macworld has a list of tips for keeping your iPhone secure.
